why: eager + absent + no default + typed: reconcile_declared/7 fails with {error, {typed_field_unset, label}} — a migration may not leave a typed slot unset (ADR 0123 § Runtime contract), and this is the failure a `late` slot must NOT hit (ADR 0124 §8/B9).
eager + absent + no default + untyped: reconcile_declared/7 fills nil — the untyped counterpart of the typed_field_unset_error row above.
eager + absent + has a default + typed: reconcile_declared/7 fills the class's own init/1 default, regardless of IsTyped — kind is eager, so the late check never applies.
eager + absent + has a default + untyped: same default-fill outcome as the typed row above — IsTyped only matters once has_default is false.

late + absent + typed: THE new row (ADR 0124 §8/B9, BT-3556) — reconcile_declared/7 leaves `proc` absent from the reconciled map entirely, checked before the typed-no-default failure the eager row above hits. `late` cannot declare a default (parse-time rejected), so has_default is always false for a late field.
late + absent + untyped: the other new row — stays absent the same way regardless of IsTyped, pinning that the kind check is not merely a typed-class special case.
late + present: kept as-is, regardless of kind — a `late` slot that was already assigned before this migration ran is untouched (the "present -> kept" branch never consults KindsMap at all).
eager + present: kept as-is — the ordinary case every other row's "absent" variant is contrasted against.
